title.value: Exploring social inequalities in healthcare trajectories following diagnosis of diabetes: a state sequence analysis of linked survey and administrative data
title.justification: This was chosen because the paper primarily investigates the healthcare trajectories following diabetes diagnosis, focusing on social inequalities and the resulting impact on healthcare access and continuity.
title.quote: Exploring social inequalities in healthcare trajectories following diagnosis of diabetes: a state sequence analysis of linked survey and administrative data.

extractions.description: The paper explores social inequalities in healthcare trajectories following a diabetes diagnosis in Quebec, Canada. It uses a state sequence analysis of the Care Trajectories-Enriched Data cohort, linking survey and administrative data to establish typologies of care trajectories and explore social determinants influencing these trajectories. Findings reveal distinct patterns of healthcare utilization that may inform the design of healthcare systems to improve patient outcomes and ensure equal access to services.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on social inequalities in healthcare access and healthcare utilization patterns following a diabetes diagnosis, not specifically addressing any aspects related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Background: Social inequalities in complications associated with diabetes mellitus persist. As a primary care sensitive condition (PCSC), this association could be related to differential access to primary care. Our objectives are to establish a typology of care trajectories following a new diagnosis, and to explore social determinants of trajectories.

primary_category.justification: The content of the paper focuses on healthcare disparities, which fall outside the specified realms of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, therefore, it does not align with any of the predefined categories related to those fields.
primary_category.quote: Our objectives are to establish a typology of care trajectories following a new diagnosis, and to explore social determinants of trajectories.

secondary_categories.justification: Since the primary focus is on social inequalities in healthcare rather than climate or ecological sustainability, there are no secondary relevant categories.
secondary_categories.quote: Introduction: The global prevalence of diabetes has been on the rise for the past several decades...Understanding the pattern of care set in motion by the diagnosis of diabetes will support the identification of care trajectories that minimize unnecessary or inappropriate services while maximizing health outcomes.

primary_sub_category.justification: This paper does not fit into any specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as it focuses primarily on healthcare trajectories and social inequalities related to diabetes.
primary_sub_category.quote: Methods: We used the TorSaDe (The Care Trajectories-Enriched Data cohort), which links Canadian Community Health Survey respondents to health administrative data.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's analysis is centered around healthcare access differences due to social factors, not directly linking to any Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-category.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Data sources: We used the Care Trajectories – Enriched Data (TorSaDE) cohort for this study, which is a linkage of Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS) and health administrative data.

applications.justification: The paper does not discuss applications in the context of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, as it focuses on healthcare access and social inequalities in healthcare.
applications.quote: Our study aimed to identify a typology of care trajectories following diabetes diagnosis and to explore sociodemographic variables associated with trajectory-type membership.

new_primary_category.justification: Since the paper focuses on social inequalities and care trajectories in healthcare, a new potential category could be 'Social Inequality in Healthcare' which would encompass studies analyzing disparities in healthcare access and utilization.
new_primary_category.quote: The paper explores social inequalities in healthcare trajectories following a diabetes diagnosis in Quebec, Canada.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: A new sub-category like 'Healthcare Trajectories and Access' would be suitable for this paper as it heavily analyzes and categorizes care trajectories and explores the social determinants affecting them.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We aimed to explore care trajectories defined by states of care as ascribed to interactions across the health care system, in order to better represent the order, timing, and continuity of care.
